abstract: Published in Science, this study analyzes over 30 million Python contributions on GitHub to measure the diffusion of AI-assisted coding. By Q4 2024, approximately 30% of Python code contributions showed evidence of AI assistance, up from near zero in early 2023. Despite this rapid adoption, the associated increase in total code output was a modest 3.6%, suggesting AI coding tools primarily substitute for rather than augment developer effort at the aggregate level.
keyFindings: 30% of Python contributions on GitHub showed AI assistance by Q4 2024
AI-assisted coding diffused rapidly from near zero to 30% in under two years
Total code output increased by only 3.6% despite widespread AI adoption
The modest output gain suggests significant substitution of human effort rather than pure augmentation
methodology: Large-scale analysis of over 30 million Python code contributions on GitHub, using statistical methods to detect AI-generated or AI-assisted code. Published in Science, tracking diffusion patterns and aggregate output effects over time.
qualifiers: Detection of AI-assisted code relies on statistical signatures that may miss some AI contributions or flag false positives. Python-specific results may not generalize to other languages. GitHub contributions are a subset of all professional software development activity.
